_title: QAL 3-BANK UNBUFFERED CHAIN: pre-registration. Written BEFORE any chain deck existed.
_written_before: No file matching chain3/c_*.cir, chain3/p_*.cir, chain3/chain.py or chain3/RESULTS.json exists at the moment this file is written. mtimes are recorded in RESULTS.json._provenance.mtimes.
_author_run: stat-sim/qal/chain3, PYMS_VAE_CACHE owned by this run (scratchpad/vae_cache_chain3, built from scratch).
THE_QUESTION: Every committed QAL hop measurement is a SINGLE hop whose gate inputs are held at ideal DC (the pull-down cells' gates at the full dV=1.0, which is ABOVE the 0.676 V rail those cells actually run on -- non-physical but trivially easy to drive). A chain has no such luxury: bank N+1's input HIGH level is whatever bank N settled to. Does the hop survive cascading, and which device binds it?

TOPOLOGY_pre_stated.buffering_between_banks: NONE. o<i> of bank N IS in<i> of bank N+1 -- the same net name. No flop, no latch, no buffer, no level shifter. A bank is a POWER DOMAIN over one level of logic.
TOPOLOGY_pre_stated.M_rationale: 8 is the committed bank size. Inputs to bank 1 alternate 1,0,1,0,... so every bank has 4 pull-UP cells (input low, output must charge to its rail) and 4 pull-DOWN cells (input high, output must hold 0) at EVERY stage -- both device types exercised at every stage. Held constant across the entire sweep.
TOPOLOGY_pre_stated.cells: sg13_lv_pmos w=1.12u l=0.13u + sg13_lv_nmos w=0.74u l=0.13u, CL 2 fF, supply AND pMOS bulk on the bank node. COMMITTED, verbatim.
TOPOLOGY_pre_stated.transfer_switch: tg15p verbatim: XSWN nMOS w=5u + XSWP pMOS w=10u (bulk to vhi=1.5 V) + XPK park nMOS w=1u from the sw node to ground, its own pk phase closing after the cut. Widths widened ONLY if the measurement demands it, and the width used is reported per row.
TOPOLOGY_pre_stated.bank_capacitance: NO explicit rail decap. Each bank IS its 8 cells. MEASURED justification: the committed CA = 35.979 fF is exactly the 8-cell bank's own secant capacitance at 1.0 V (swsweep/sw_calib.cir.prn integrates Q_sup(1.0 V) = 35.983 fC), so a chain of identical 8-cell banks is capacitance-MATCHED by construction, exactly as the committed single hop was, and L = 277.8 nH keeps its meaning as the known-good anchor.
symmetry_devices: Each bank carries an identical SUPPLY transmission gate (tg15p sizing) to an ideal dV rail. Bank 1's is the chain head (it pre-charges bank 1 to dV and OPENS before hop 1, so bank 1 starts genuinely settled with exactly Q(dV) on it, which a bare .ic cannot do -- the cells would charge their own outputs out of their own rail and drop it ~0.22 V before the hop). Banks 2 and 3 have the same device: DISABLED in the free-running chain, ENABLED in the top-up chain. So the free and top-up curves have IDENTICAL topology and differ only by an enable.

Bank 1 also carries a DUMMY incoming transfer switch, gate held off and park held on, so all three rails carry exactly one switch drain terminal. Without it hop 1 would transfer from a lighter source into a heavier destination and would not be representative of a steady-state pipeline stage.
TOPOLOGY_pre_stated.ideal_sources_in_the_deck: bank 1's 8 gate inputs (the chain head -- legitimate), the dV supply rail, vhi = 1.5 V, and the switch gate phases. NOTHING else.

SEQUENCING_pre_stated.rule: Sequencing IS the wave. hop k closes at T_k, opens at its OWN re-probed true current zero t_zcs(k). hop 2 closes at T2 = T1 + t_zcs(1) + DELTA(L).
SEQUENCING_pre_stated.DELTA_definition: DELTA(L) = ceil(t_valid90(L) - t_hop(L)) ps taken from the COMMITTED single-hop L sweep (qal/lsweep/rows.json, same L, same switch width), floored at 4 ps = 2*edge. This is a PRIOR measurement, not a chain measurement, so the stagger is not tuned on the result it is testing.
SEQUENCING_pre_stated.why_this_DELTA: It gives each chain stage EXACTLY the time the single hop needed at that L (t_hop + lag = the committed t_level). So the chain at L is handed the single hop's own stage time and the pass/fail is a like-for-like test of whether that speed survives cascading.
SEQUENCING_pre_stated.pre_roll: T1 = 200 ps. Bank 1's measured settling at T1 is reported; if it is not >=99.9% the pre-roll is lengthened and that is stated.
SEQUENCING_pre_stated.tail: hop2_open + DELTA(L) + 500 ps, so bank 3 gets the same stage allowance as its predecessors AND an eventual-settle reading.

ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.A1_settling: EVERY gate in EVERY one of the three banks settles >= 90% at its OWN stage-boundary checkpoint. Reported per gate, never aggregated.
ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.A1_checkpoints: Bank k's checkpoint is the instant its SUCCESSOR's transfer switch CLOSES, i.e. the instant bank k's data is actually sampled: bank 1 -> T1_close, bank 2 -> T2_close. Bank 3 -> hop2_open + DELTA(L), the same stage allowance its predecessors got.
ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.A1_convention: COMMITTED convention: pull-UP cell (input low) s = V(o)/V(rail_k); pull-DOWN cell (input high) s = 1 - V(o)/V(rail_k); V(rail_k) is the INSTANTANEOUS rail of that cell's own bank at the checkpoint.
ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.A2_margin_budget: Total delivered-rail depression <= 120 mV, charged BOTH ways and both reported: (i) CUMULATIVE from the committed single-hop reference delivered rail VBEND_ref = 0.6759 V -> absolute floor 0.5559 V for every bank; (ii) COMPOUNDING-ONLY, VBEND2 - VBEND3 <= 120 mV. Sub-allowance reported separately: the cliff floor VBEND >= 0.600 V (the committed C3 gate, whose stated rationale is that the cell pMOS stops clearing |Vtp| below it).
ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.A2_budget_provenance: 120 mV = the ~76 mV cliff allowance implied by the committed C3 gate (0.6759 -> 0.600) plus the 44 mV recycle loss MEASURED in the committed two-bank recycle row (qal/README.md: 'recycle only 0.556 V (-44 mV)'). Chain compounding has never been charged against it before; this run charges it.
ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.A3_instrument: Per hop, the energy path identity ea - esw - er = dE_L must vanish at that hop's OWN current zero: |ea_k - esw_k - er_k| <= 0.02 fJ at t_zcs(k) (committed AMENDMENT A1 -- the identity holds at the ZERO, not at the post-open checkpoint). Every 1F integrator is t0-referenced at a 0.5 ps Z checkpoint (the campaign's pedestal trap). Plus the committed anchor reproduced digit-for-digit before any chain deck is run.
ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.A4_rail_drain_completeness: Committed C2: VA_open <= 0.1478 * (that hop's source rail). Reported per hop; it is the criterion that decides whether the transfer switch is widened.
ACCEPTANCE_all_must_hold.VERDICT_rule: A row is FUNCTIONAL only if A1 and A2(i) and A3 hold. A2(ii), the cliff sub-allowance and A4 are reported and discussed but do not by themselves void a row; any row that fails them is flagged.

PRE_STATED_CALL_which_device_limits.primary: STAGE 2 BECOMES nMOS PULL-DOWN LIMITED. In the single hop the pull-down cells' gates were held at the full dV = 1.0 V while their own bank ran at a 0.676 V rail -- about 0.5 V of nMOS overdrive, non-physical and trivially easy. In the chain those gates get only bank 1's settled output, so about 0.676 V against a measured Vtn of roughly 0.4-0.5 V: about 0.18-0.27 V of overdrive, a ~2.5x reduction. The pMOS pull-up's condition is UNCHANGED from the single hop (its gate is a real logic 0 either way); it degrades only through rail droop.
PRE_STATED_CALL_which_device_limits.primary_evidence_that_would_confirm_it: min settling among bank 2's four pull-DOWN cells < min settling among bank 2's four pull-UP cells at the stage-2 checkpoint -- a REVERSAL of the committed single hop, where the pull-UP group was the laggard (81.9% at the open checkpoint) and the pull-DOWN group sat at 100.07%.
PRE_STATED_CALL_which_device_limits.secondary: STAGE 3 REVERTS TO pMOS PULL-UP LIMITED once its delivered rail falls below about 0.60 V, because that is the documented functional cliff (the pull-up cannot clear |Vtp| ~ 0.50 V). Pre-stated crossover: delivered rail ~ 0.60 V.
PRE_STATED_CALL_which_device_limits.falsifier: If at every stage and every L the pull-UP group is still the laggard and the pull-down group stays >= 99%, the primary call is WRONG and the chain's binding device is the same pMOS pull-up the single hop had -- i.e. the ideal-DC-input flattery did not matter.

PRE_STATED_QUANTITATIVE_PREDICTIONS.the_recorded_droop_will_not_reproduce: The record's -0.56%/hop (qal_a1f_chain.py, qal_a1f_chain_bare.cir) was MEASURED on an IDEAL LC chain: 6 linear 10 fF caps, behavioral VSWITCH RON=1 ohm, L=1 uH, R=100 ohm, Q~141, dV=0.6, total loss 0.097 fJ over 5 hops, NO DEVICES AND NO GATES AT ALL. The real committed hop loses 8.383 fJ out of ~18 fJ stored, of which ~6.65 fJ is switch-related and only 0.050 fJ is I^2R. -0.56%/hop is an I^2R-only number and cannot survive real devices.
PRE_STATED_QUANTITATIVE_PREDICTIONS.predicted_per_hop_droop: DERIVED from the committed charge books: the tg15p switch absorbs about 8.2 fC per hop (Q through L at the open checkpoint 32.48 fC vs the destination bank's own Q(0.676 V) = 24.30 fC from the calib curve) and the source retains VA_open * C ~ 3.5 fC. Against a MEASURED incremental bank capacitance of 36.6 fF at the operating point, that is about 220 + 100 mV of rail lost per hop: predicted -25% to -33% per hop, roughly 50x worse than the recorded -0.56%/hop.
PRE_STATED_QUANTITATIVE_PREDICTIONS.predicted_budget_outcome: The FREE-RUNNING chain busts the 120 mV budget on the FIRST hop, at every L. If that is what happens, the headline is a NEGATIVE result -- the free-running unbuffered chain does not hold together at any L -- and the top-up is not an optional extra but a REQUIREMENT, so the headline L becomes the fastest L at which the TOPPED-UP chain settles, and the top-up energy is the price of the throughput claim.
PRE_STATED_QUANTITATIVE_PREDICTIONS.predicted_headline_direction: The chain's fastest sustainable L is SLOWER than the single hop's, because droop compounds and the cell settling lag is L-independent (~25 ps) while the stage time shrinks as sqrt(L).

SINGLE_HOP_COMPARATOR_frozen_now._source: qal/lsweep/rows.json, the committed Track-1 L sweep. Frozen here so the chain cannot be compared against a moving target.

L_GRID_pre_stated.anchor: 277.8 nH is run FIRST as the known-good slow point (stage c). If the chain does not settle at all three stages there, or the measured per-hop droop is not explicable, the HARNESS is fixed before any L is swept.
L_GRID_pre_stated.widening: If a row fails A4 (rail-drain completeness) the same L is re-run at total_um 30 and, if needed, 60, and the width used is reported per row. Widening is MEASURED, in the committed sweep, to trade VBEND away for VA_open, so for a chain it is not free and is not applied pre-emptively.
L_GRID_pre_stated.zero_re_probe: MANDATORY at every point and for EVERY hop separately: the analytic pi*sqrt(LC) value was measured 36% early with real gate loads, and the chain's second hop sees a different source level and a different destination load than the first. Probe protocol: probe A = hop 1 closes and never opens, hop 2 held off -> first I(L1) downward zero after the I(L1) peak = t_zcs(1). probe B = hop 1 cut at t_zcs(1) + park, hop 2 closes at T2 and never opens -> first I(L2) downward zero after its peak = t_zcs(2). Then the measured deck cuts both at their own zeros.

TOPUP_pre_stated.mechanism: Enable bank k's supply transmission gate (the SAME device already present and disabled in the free-running deck) for a window inside the inter-hop gap, closing it before that bank's own hop. It restores the bank to the dV rail, supplying only the deficit.
TOPUP_pre_stated.cost_metric: Q_topup and E_topup = dV * Q_topup per bank per hop, from a 1F integrator on the dV source current, t0-referenced. Exact, because the supply is a constant-voltage source. Reported per bank and as a chain total, alongside the free-running numbers. Energy is NOT the gate for this run, but the cost is reported so it is not hidden.
TOPUP_pre_stated.risk_stated_now: The top-up is RESISTIVE through a device, inside a gap only tens of ps wide. If it cannot complete in the gap, the device is widened and the width is reported -- and the widening adds capacitance to every bank, which is itself a cost and is reported as a shift in t_zcs.
TOPUP_pre_stated.control_run: At L = 277.8 nH the chain is ALSO run with the supply TGs physically absent, to separate the supply device's capacitance from the top-up's effect.

HEADLINE_definition_pre_stated: The FASTEST L at which every gate in all three banks still settles >= 90% at its own stage-boundary checkpoint AND the chain stays inside the 120 mV margin budget -- reported for the free-running chain and for the topped-up chain separately -- compared against the frozen single-hop comparator above (best single-hop t_level 176.87 ps at L = 45 nH, W = 15 um). If the chain's limit is slower, THAT DIFFERENCE IS THE FINDING and it is the number a throughput claim has to use.

HONESTY_clauses.lower_bound: sg13lv_compat.sp ZEROES ad/as/pd/ps, so junction capacitance is ABSENT everywhere. Every capacitance, every energy and every delay in this run is therefore a LOWER BOUND / optimistic. That matters MORE for a chain than for a single hop, because the missing drain junction cap is part of the load bank N drives into bank N+1 and part of what holds bank N's output up after its rail collapses.
HONESTY_clauses.labels: Every reported number is labelled MEASURED, DERIVED or ASSUMED.
HONESTY_clauses.negative_results: A negative result is first-class. 'The chain does not hold together below L = X' and 'the chain does not hold together at ANY L without top-up' are both acceptable, reportable outcomes and neither will be dressed up.
HONESTY_clauses.no_self_baseline: The single-hop comparator is the COMMITTED lsweep table, frozen above, not re-derived by this run.
HONESTY_clauses.what_would_make_this_run_worthless: A chain that looks like it settles because it is not actually computing (e.g. a bank whose inputs never change, or a settling metric taken against a rail that has already collapsed so the ratio is trivially ~1). Guard: every bank's four pull-UP outputs must be measured HIGH (>= 0.5 * its rail) and its four pull-DOWN outputs measured LOW (<= 0.1 * its rail) at its checkpoint, i.e. the DATA PATTERN must be verified present at every stage, and that check is reported as its own row field.
